newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WI optimistic on Australia wool price rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WI optimistic on Australia wool price rise.

text.p: Australian wool industry statutory authority Wool International (WI) said it has increased its forecast average 1996/97 eastern market wool price indicator to 620 cents a kg clean from 600.

The increase was based on expectations of a higher anticipated first quarter average than previously forecast, WI said in its Insight journal. Further improvement was expected later in the season, it said.
WI said the market indicator rose steadily during August, with the month's closing level of 615 cents/kg clean, up 22 cents on the month before, its highest level since January 1996.
Still, at the end of August, the indicator was 100 cents below its year-earlier level, WI said.
Economic and retail conditions were mixed, with U.S. and Japanese indicators strong and the risk of Western European growth underperforming, it said.
Inter-fibre price competition was likely to intensify over the season, it said.
Trade clearances of Australian wool were expected to be significantly higher in 1996/97, capping potential price rises. Prospects appeared strongest for fine wool, WI said.
The top three export destinations for Australian raw wool in 1995/96 remained unchanged from the previous season, WI said.
China/Hong Kong remained the leading export market in volume and value terms, taking 180 million kg greasy equivalent, up two percent on 1994/95.
Italy was the second largest export destination in 1995/96 taking 104 million kg greasy equivalent, four percent lower than a year earlier.
Exports to Japan, the third-largest destination, fell by 31 percent, the largest fall among the top 10 destinations.
Australia's raw wool exports fell by seven percent to 697 million kg greasy equivalent in 1995/96, the lowest level since the collapse of the reserve price scheme in 1990/91, WI said.
